semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {وَضُحَاهَا}: The discussion of this root has already been given in [Sūrat] «Ṭā Hā». Al-Mubarrad said: «الضُّحى and الضَّحْوة are both derived from الضَّحّ, which is light; the alif and the wāw were substituted for the ḥāʾ.» This almost amounts to a fabrication against someone like Abū al-ʿAbbās, given his eminence.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {يَغْشَاهَا}: The object [pronoun] is for the sun; it was also said: for the earth. «يَغْشاها» was brought as an imperfect, unlike what precedes and follows it, out of regard for the verse-endings (fawāṣil); for had it been brought as a past, the construction would be «إذا غَشِيَها», and the verbal correspondence between the verse-endings and the cadences would be lost.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {وَمَا بَنَاهَا} and what follows it contain two views. The first: «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي» (who/which); those who permit its being used for individual rational beings cited it as evidence, because what is meant by it is the Creator, Exalted is He. Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Abū ʿUbayda held this, and Ibn Jarīr chose it. The second: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "and the building of the heaven"; al-Zajjāj and al-Mubarrad held this, based on their view that it is restricted to non-rational beings. This view was objected to on the grounds that it would entail the oath being by the verbal nouns themselves: the building of the heaven, the spreading of the earth and the fashioning of the soul, whereas what is intended is only the oath by the doer of these things, namely the Lord, Blessed and Exalted. Two answers were given to this. The first: it is by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "and by the Lord of — or the Builder of — the building of the heaven", and the like. The second: there is nothing strange in swearing by these things, just as He the Exalted swore by the morning and the like.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It was made maṣdariyya, but this is not the right view, because of His saying "فأَلْهمها" and the corruption of the composition it leads to. The right view is that it is relative; it was preferred to "مَنْ" only to convey the meaning of description, as if it were said: and by the heaven and the Mighty, Powerful One Who built it, and by a soul and the Wise One of dazzling wisdom Who fashioned it. And among their sayings is: "سبحانَ ما سَخَّرَكُنَّ لنا" (Glory be to Him Who subjected you to us).» End of quotation. He means that the fāʿil (agent) in «فألهمها» refers to Allah the Exalted, so let it be so in «بناها» too; and then it must refer back to something, and there is nothing here to which it could refer except «ما», so it is determined that it is relative.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «As for his saying: "it is not the right view because of His saying فَأَلْهمها", he means the reference of the pronoun in "فَأَلْهمها" to Allah the Exalted, so that it would refer to something mentioned, namely "ما" meant as "الذي". This does not follow, because if we make it maṣdariyya, the pronoun refers to what is understood from the context of the speech; so in "بناها" there is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, i.e. "and His building it", i.e. Allah the Exalted; just as, when you see Zayd having struck ʿAmr, you say: "عجبتُ مِمَّا ضَرَبَ عمراً", its implied form being: "at his striking ʿAmr" — this would be good, eloquent and permissible; and the reference of a pronoun to what is understood from the context of speech is frequent. And his saying: "and the corruption of the composition it leads to" is not so; making it maṣdariyya does not lead to what he mentioned. And his saying: "it was preferred only…" to the end — neither the relative "ما" nor the relative "مَنْ" conveys the meaning of description, because neither is used as an adjective, unlike "الذي"; so their sharing in not conveying the meaning of description is present in both, and "ما" does not have it to the exclusion of "مَنْ". And his saying: "and among their sayings…" to the end — our colleagues interpreted it as "سبحان" being a proper name and "ما" being maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (temporal-verbal).» End of quotation.
As for his rebuttal of him by [the pronoun's] referring to what is understood from the context, it is not suitable as a rebuttal, because when the matter wavers between its referring to something expressed and something not expressed, its referring to what is expressed is preferable, because that is the basic rule. As for his saying: "so «ما» does not have it to the exclusion of «مَنْ»", al-Zamakhsharī does not mean that it is used as an explicit adjective; rather, he means that it applies to the kind of rational beings and to their attribute; that is why the grammarians illustrated it with His saying: {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 3], and they said: its implied form is "so marry the good among women"; and there is no doubt that «ما» has this rule to the exclusion of «مَنْ». The indefiniteness of «نفس»: either it is to magnify it, i.e. a mighty soul, namely the soul of Ādam, or for multiplicity, as in His saying: {عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ} [al-Infiṭār: 5].

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {جَلاَّهَا}: The agent is a pronoun referring to the day (النهار). It was also said: it refers to Allah the Exalted. The accusative pronoun refers either to the sun, or to the darkness, or to the world (al-dunyā), or to the earth.

His saying: {إِذَا تَلاَهَا} and what follows it contain a difficulty. For if it is made conditional, it requires an apodosis, and there is no apodosis in the wording, and supplying one is not suitable. And if it is made a pure adverb, it calls for a governor, and there is no governor here except the verb of the oath; yet making it govern is problematic, because the verb of the oath is of the present (ḥāl), being a performative (inshāʾ), while «إذا» is an adverb of the future, and the present does not govern the future. The answer to this, and its verification, will come when I mention its probing and division (sabr and taqsīm) shortly, if Allah the Exalted wills.

The second «إذا» and what follows it have a further difficulty of their own, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī, in which there is some obscurity, so take note of it. He said: "If you say: the matter of the accusative of «إذا» is baffling, because you cannot avoid one of two things. Either you make the wāws conjunctions, so that they cause accusative and genitive and you fall into conjunction upon two governors, as in your saying «مررتُ أمسِ بزيدٍ واليومَ عمروٍ» ("I passed yesterday by Zayd and today ʿAmr"); or you make them wāws of oath, so that you fall into what al-Khalīl and Sībawayh agreed to dislike. I say: the answer is that with the wāw of oath, expressing the verb is dropped altogether. So it has a status unlike that of the bāʾ, where the verb is expressed with it and also omitted; the wāw stands in the place of the verb, while the bāʾ fills the place of both together. The conjunctive wāws are deputies of this wāw, and so they rightly act as governors with the action of the verb and the preposition together, as you say «ضربَ زيدٌ عمراً وبكرٌ خالداً» ("Zayd struck ʿAmr and Bakr Khālid"), where you make nominative and accusative by the wāw, because it stands in the place of «ضرب», which is the governor of both." End of quotation.

The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for his saying about the conjunctive wāws 'so that they cause accusative and genitive': this is not the preferred view, I mean that the conjunction particle should govern by standing in the place of the governor. Rather, the preferred view is that the government belongs to the governor of the word conjoined to, and we do not dispute with him over that. As for his saying 'so you fall into conjunction upon two governors': what is in the verse is not conjunction upon two governors. It belongs rather to the chapter of conjoining two nouns, one genitive and one accusative, to two nouns, one genitive and one accusative, so the conjunction particle did not stand in for two governors. That is like your saying «امرُرْ بزيدٍ قائماً وعمروٍ جالساً» ("Pass by Zayd standing and ʿAmr sitting"). And Sībawayh recited in his book:

4578 - وليس بمعروفٍ لنا أَنْ نَرُدَّها ... صِحاحاً ولا مُسْتَنْكرٍ أن تُعَقَّرا
(It is not known among us that we return them sound, nor is it unheard of that they be hamstrung)

This is a conjunction of a genitive and a nominative upon a genitive and a nominative. Concerning conjunction upon two governors there are four doctrines, and permissibility is attributed to Sībawayh. As for his saying 'and in your saying «مررْتُ أمسِ بزيدٍ واليومَ عمروٍ»': this example differs from what is in the verse; rather the counterpart of what is in the verse is «مررْتُ بزيدٍ أمسٍ وعمروٍ اليومَ», and we permit this. As for his saying 'what al-Khalīl and Sībawayh agreed to dislike': it is not as he said; rather the speech of al-Khalīl indicates prohibition. Al-Khalīl said, concerning the saying of the Mighty and Exalted:

{والليل إِذَا يغشى والنهار إِذَا تجلى وَمَا خَلَقَ الذكر والأنثى} [al-Layl: 13]

'The last two wāws are not on the level of the first. They are the two wāws that join nouns to nouns, as in your saying «مررتُ بزيدٍ وعمرو», whereas the first is on the level of the tāʾ and the bāʾ.' As for his saying that the wāw of oath is one with which expressing the verb is dropped altogether: this ruling is not agreed upon; rather Ibn Kaysān permitted stating the verb of the oath with the wāw, so you say «أُقْسِم» or «أَحْلِفُ» «واللَّهِ لَزيدٌ قائمٌ». And as for his saying 'the conjunctive wāws are deputies of this one' to the end: it is built on the claim that the conjunction particle governs because it stands in for the governor, and that is not the preferred view." He said: "What we say is that the baffling thing is supplying the governor of «إذا» after the oaths, as in His saying {والنجم إِذَا هوى} [al-Najm: 1], {والليل إِذْ أَدْبَرَ} [al-Muddaththir: 33], {والصبح إِذَآ أَسْفَرَ} [al-Muddaththir: 34], {والقمر إِذَا تَلاَهَا}, {والليل إِذَا يغشى} [al-Layl: 1], and the like. For «إذا» is an adverb of the future. It cannot be that its governor is the omitted verb of the oath, because that is a performative verb and so is of the present, and it is incompatible for it to govern the future, owing to the difference between the time of the governor and the time of the governed. Nor can there be an omitted muḍāf with the thing sworn by standing in its place, i.e. 'and by the rising of the star and the coming of the night', because that is governed by that verb; the rising is of the present, and it does not govern the future, since of necessity the time of the governor is the time of the governed. Nor can the thing sworn by itself govern it, because it is not among the things that govern, especially if it is a body. Nor can an omitted word be supplied before the adverb so that it governs it, that governor being in the position of a ḥāl, its implied form being 'by the star, being [there] when it falls; by the night, being [there] when it covers', because it would follow that «كائناً» has no governor to put it in the accusative, and it cannot be governed by any of the things we supposed to be governors. Moreover the thing sworn by may be a body, and adverbs of time cannot be ḥāls of bodies, just as they cannot be predicates." End of what the Shaykh used in refutation, and of what he found problematic regarding the governor of «إذا». And I, praise be to Allah, shall follow his statements and make clear what is in them.

[The author:] As for his saying "the preferred view is that the conjunction particle does not govern by standing in the place of the governor": this does not bind Abū al-Qāsim [Translator's note: al-Zamakhsharī], because he prefers the other view. As for his saying "what is in this verse is not conjunction upon two governors": that is disputed; rather it does contain conjunction upon two governors, though with some obscurity. The explanation that it is conjunction upon two governors is as follows: His saying {والنهار إِذَا جَلاَّهَا} has here two governed words, one genitive, namely «النهار», and the other accusative, namely the adverb. This is a conjunction upon the two governed words of two governors, the two governors being the verb of the oath which puts the first «إذا» in the accusative, and the wāw of oath which causes the genitive. So you have two governors, each with a governed word. When you conjoin a genitive to a genitive and an adverb to an adverb, as two governed words of two governors, what Abū al-Qāsim said follows. How could this be missed by anyone who reflects and verifies?

As for his saying "and Sībawayh recited …" to the end: that is an admission from him that it is a case of conjunction upon two governors; the most he did was to lean on the standing of Sībawayh.

As for his saying "Ibn Kaysān permitted …": his doctrine does not bind al-Zamakhsharī. As for his saying "the example corresponds to the verse; rather its counterpart is …" to the end: that is correct, because in it the second adverb is put before the conjoined genitive, whereas in the verse the adverb comes later. But what al-Zamakhsharī means is the existence of two governed words of two governors, and that exists in the example he mentioned, except that it has another difficulty, namely that it is like a repetition of the issue.

As for his saying "rather the speech of al-Khalīl indicates prohibition" to the end: there is no refutation of him in it with regard to what he intended; rather it strengthens what he said. The most there is, is that he expressed prohibition by "dislike," or did not understand the prohibition. As for his saying "nor can there be an omitted muḍāf" to the end, I say: rather, supplying it is permissible, and it is the governor, and the difference of the two times that he claimed does not follow. For it is permissible to swear now by the rising of the star in the future, so the oath is in the present and the rising in the future; and it is permissible to swear by something that will come into existence. As for his saying "nor can an omitted word be supplied before the adverb so that it governs it" to the end: that is not prohibited; rather it is permissible, and it is an implied (muqaddara) ḥāl. As for his saying "it would follow that it has no governor": it is not so; rather it has a governor, namely the verb of the oath, and its being a performative does no harm, because the ḥāl is implied, as already stated. As for his saying "the thing sworn by may be a body": the answer is that an event is then supplied of which the adverb of time is a ḥāl. This question was put to the Shaykh Abū ʿAmr Ibn al-Ḥājib, who refined the question and answered along the lines of what I mentioned. And Allah knows best. Yet the discussion of it is not free of dispute and long debate with him.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ}: There are two views on it. One: that it is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), the original being «لقد», and the lām was omitted only because of the length of the speech. The second: that it is not an answer, but was brought as a follower to His saying {فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا} by way of digression (istiṭrād), and is in no way part of the answer to the oath. The answer is then omitted, its implied form being «ليُدَمْدِمَنَّ اللَّهُ عليهم» ("Allah will surely crush them"), i.e. the people of Mecca, for their denial of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, just as He crushed Thamūd for their denial of Ṣāliḥ, peace be upon him. Al-Zamakhsharī gave this sense, while others supplied «لتُبْعَثُنَّ» ("you will surely be resurrected").

And His saying: {طَحَاهَا} [al-Shams: 3], i.e. «دَحاها» ("spread it out"); its meaning has already been given. It has two forms: one says «طحا يَطْحوا» and «طحى يَطْحي». «طحا» also comes in the sense of "went away". ʿAlqama said:

4579 - طحابك قَلْبٌ في الحِسانِ طَروبُ ... بُعَيْدَ الشبابِ عَصْرَ حان مَشيبُ
(A heart addicted to fair women has carried you away, just after youth, at the time when grey hair has come)

It is also said that «طحا» means "rose high". Among their oaths is «ولا والقمرِ الطَّاحي», i.e. "the one rising high". As for the agent of «زكَّاها» and «دَسَّاها», the apparent sense is that it is the pronoun of «مَنْ». It was also said: it is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, i.e. "whoever Allah purified" and "whoever Allah corrupted," meaning: whoever Allah has purified his soul. Al-Zamakhsharī attacked the holder of this view because it clashes with his own school. The truth is that it is contrary to the apparent sense, not for the reason al-Zamakhsharī gave, but because it clashes with the structure of the wording, since it requires the pronoun to return to the soul as qualified by its being annexed to the pronoun of «مَنْ»

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {دَسَّاهَا}: Its origin is «دسَّسَهَا». The like letters became too many, so a weak letter was substituted for the third of them, as they said «قَصَّيْتُ [أَظْفاري]» ("I trimmed my nails") and [in the saying]:

4580 - تَقَضِّيَ البازِي. . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The swooping of the falcon … [the rest of the verse is omitted in the source])

[Translator's note: the rest of the verse is left blank with dots in the source.] And «التَّدْسِيَةُ» is concealment, meaning: he concealed it with immorality. The original form was actually pronounced by the one who said:

4581 - وأنت الذي دَسَّسْتَ عمراً فأصبحَتْ ... حَلائلُه منه أراملَ ضُيَّعاً
(It was you who buried ʿAmr, so his wives became, because of it, widows, forsaken)

and by the one who said:

4582 - ودَسَّسْت عَمْراً في التراب فأصبحَتْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And I buried ʿAmr in the dust, so … [the rest is omitted in the source])

the verse [in full].

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {بِطَغْوَاهَآ}: This bāʾ has three possible senses. The first: that it is the bāʾ of instrumentality (istiʿāna) in a figurative sense, as in "I wrote with the pen." Al-Zamakhsharī began with this, and he means: it denied by means of its transgression, as you say, "He wronged me by his audacity against Allah the Exalted." The second: that it is a bāʾ of transitivity (taʿdiya), i.e. it denied what it was threatened with, namely its punishment, the punishment of transgression, as in His saying, the Exalted, {فَأُهْلِكُواْ بالطاغية} [al-Ḥāqqa: 5]. The third: that it is for causation, i.e. because of its transgression.

The majority read «طَغْواها» with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ; it is a maṣdar meaning «الطُّغيان» ("transgression"). The yāʾ was turned into a wāw only in order to distinguish the noun from the adjective. That is, they keep the yāʾ of the pattern fa‘lā with fatḥa when it is an adjective, such as «خَزْيا» and «صَدْيا», and they change it in the noun, such as «تَقْوى» and «شَرْوى». The yāʾ was kept in the adjective because the adjective is heavier than the noun, and the yāʾ is lighter than the wāw, so it was placed in the heavier.

Al-Ḥasan, Muḥammad b. Kaʿb and Ḥammād read it with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ; this too is a maṣdar like «الرُّجْعى» and «الحُسْنى», except that it is irregular (shādhdh), since by right the yāʾ should have stayed as it is, like «السُّقْيا» and its like. All this holds for those who say «طَغَيْتُ طُغْياناً» with yāʾ. As for those who say «طَغَوْت» with wāw, for them the wāw is the original. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The discussion of the two dialects has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara, and praise be to Allah.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {إِذِ انبعث}: «إذِ» admits two analyses. One: that it is an adverb attached to «كذَّبَتْ». The second: that it is an adverb attached to «الطَّغْوى».

«أشْقاها» is the agent of «انبعَث». It has two views. One: that a single, specific person is meant. In the exegesis it is a man called Qudār b. Sālif. The second: that a group is meant. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be that they were a group, and the singular is because you treat the singular and the plural, the masculine and the feminine, alike in the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) when you annex it. It would have been possible to say «أشْقَوْها»." End of quotation. He ought to have qualified it by saying "when you annex it to a definite noun," because the ruling for an elative annexed to an indefinite noun is the singular and the masculine in every case, like the one accompanied by «مِنْ».

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {فَقَالَ لَهُمْ}: If «أَشْقاها» means a group, the return of the pronoun in «لهم» to them is clear; if it means a specific individual, then the pronoun in «لهم» refers to Thamūd.

His saying: {نَاقَةَ الله} is accusative as a warning (taḥdhīr), i.e. "beware of the she-camel of Allah, and do not approach her." Omitting the governing verb is obligatory here because of the conjunction, for omitting the governor is obligatory in three places. First: when the one warned against is of the type «إيّاك» and its class. Second: when a conjunction is present. Third: when a repetition is present, such as «الأسدَ الأسدَ».

Zayd b. ʿAlī read «ناقةُ الله» in the nominative, as the predicate of an implied subject, i.e. "this is the she-camel of Allah, so do not expose yourselves to her."

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {فَدَمْدَمَ}: As for «الدَّمْدَمَةُ», it was said: it is covering over; one says «دَمْدَمْتُ عليه القبرَ», i.e. "I covered the grave over him." It was said: it is pressing to the ground. It was said: destruction by uprooting. It was said: «الدَّمْدَمَةُ» is an imitation of the sound of a crash, and from it comes «دَمْدَمَ في كلامه» ("he muttered in his speech"). And «دَمْدَمْتُ الثوبَ» means "I coated the garment with dye." The bāʾ in «بذَنْبهم» is for causation.

His saying: {فَسَوَّاهَا}: The accusative pronoun may refer to Thamūd, regarded as a tribe, as it was made to refer in His saying «بَطَغْواها»; and it may refer to the crushing and the punishment, i.e. "He made it equal among them," so none of them escaped. Ibn al-Zubayr read «فَدَهْدَمَ», with a hāʾ between the two dāls in place of the mīm, which means the same as the well-known reading.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {وَلاَ يَخَافُ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «فلا» with fāʾ, and the others with wāw. It is written with fāʾ in the copies of Medina and Syria and with wāw in the others, so each read according to what agrees with the script of his own codex. It is reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to read «ولم يَخَفْ», which supports the reading with wāw; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. The fāʾ requires sequence, which is obvious. The wāw may be for ḥāl, or for resuming the report. The agent pronoun in «يَخاف» may refer to the Lord, which is the most apparent, as He is the nearest one mentioned. The second: that it refers to the Messenger of Allah, i.e. "and he does not fear the outcome of this punishment, because of his warning them." The third: that it refers to «أشقاها», i.e. "he rose to hamstring her, while he did not fear the consequence of this vile deed." The «عقبى» of a thing is its end.
